items.meaning: Students register in a 48-hour window per year of study, year 4 first.
Prerequisites are checked at registration and the missing ones are listed.
Courses have a capacity; the waiting list promotes automatically by timestamp when a seat opens.
A timetable clash warns but registration is still allowed with the dean's approval.
A student can drop a course until week 3 without a transcript mark.
Advisors see their students' registrations and can hold one pending a meeting.
Erasmus students use the same system with a provisional student id.
A student with unpaid fees from last semester cannot register.
Registration confirmation PDF with the courses and the timetable.
Nightly xlsx export of enrolment per course to the department secretaries.
Audit log of every registration change, who and when, kept 5 years.
Course description page with ECTS, lecturer, language and assessment method.
The system holds 3,000 concurrent registrations in the first hour of the window.

must_not_invent: a mobile app (REG-114 is Won't do)
fixing the old system crash (REG-106 is a bug, not a requirement)
password reset emails (REG-111 is a bug)
grades or transcripts beyond the drop rule
notes: Statuses matter: Bug rows and the Won't do row are not items; the Closed-Duplicate row folds into G07-02. Thirteen items from seventeen rows. The model must not convert "Won't do" into a Not needed item on the list; it is excluded from the list.
